meta.title: Decision Register — Questions, Information gaps and Answers
meta.rule: A question may only be marked 'answered' when the answer is verified against an official source and that source is linked. Anything else stays open.

questions.question: Do we have the legal right to ingest and republish NFL play-by-play, snap counts and historical odds?
questions.why_it_blocks: Every model, backtest and correlation value depends on this. Without it, only the officially published aggregates may be shown.
questions.known_information: The NFL's exclusive data distribution partner for official league data to media and to licensed sportsbook operators is Sportradar (announced 2015; expanded 2019).
questions.what_would_answer_it: A signed data agreement, or a documented decision to operate only on public official pages.
questions.source_note: NFL.com confirms the league's integrity/education posture; the Sportradar exclusivity is reported by the league's press coverage, not by an NFL.com page we could fetch.

questions.question: Which licensed feed supplies historical closing lines, and at what granularity (book, time, limit)?
questions.why_it_blocks: Without a market benchmark there is no way to compute edge, expected value, or closing-line value. A strategy cannot be scored.
questions.known_information: No odds feed exists in this repository. No historical price is stored anywhere.
questions.what_would_answer_it: A named vendor, contract terms, and the retention rules for quotes.
questions.source_note: NFL.com's own picks page attributes odds to a commercial sportsbook and timestamps them — evidence that any official-page odds are a third-party snapshot, not a league feed.

questions.question: What exact settlement rules apply to each market we originate (push, void, overtime, stat corrections)?
questions.why_it_blocks: A probability cannot be graded without a settlement rule. Two books with different void policies produce two different fair prices for the same bet.
questions.known_information: No settlement specification exists in the repository.
questions.what_would_answer_it: A house rulebook adopted before any strategy is registered.
questions.source_note: The official 2026 NFL Rulebook defines game outcomes (including overtime and ties) but says nothing about wagering settlement — settlement is a book-level contract.

questions.question: Can we obtain licensed snap counts per player per game?
questions.why_it_blocks: The 'who is actually playing, and is the backup already on the field' model in the Availability methodology cannot be computed without it.
questions.known_information: Official gamebooks publish participation, but no machine-readable licensed feed is in the repo.
questions.what_would_answer_it: Snap-count data under license plus a documented join to the official injury report.
questions.source_note: The official Week 10 injury report prints practice/game status only; it contains no participation or snap data.

questions.question: Is a club-published, self-labelled 'unofficial' depth chart sufficient to call a player a starter?
questions.why_it_blocks: The entire 2nd/3rd/4th-string analysis rests on this definition.
questions.known_information: The league publishes no league-wide depth chart. Clubs publish their own, and at least Detroit and Green Bay print 'unofficial' on the page.
questions.what_would_answer_it: An owner decision on the definition, recorded here with the chosen tier.
questions.source_note: Page is titled '2026 Unofficial Depth Chart Compiled by Lions Football Communications'.

questions.question: How often is the official injury report captured, and what timestamp governs a forecast?
questions.why_it_blocks: If the cutoff is fuzzy, look-ahead leaks into the backtest and the strategy's edge is an artefact.
questions.known_information: The official report changes across the practice week (Wednesday/Thursday/Friday) and again at inactives.
questions.what_would_answer_it: A scheduled capture with stored retrieval timestamps, and a declared cut-off per week.
questions.source_note: Report is organised by practice day, confirming the values change within a week.

questions.question: What funds the leaderboard rewards, who is eligible, and in which jurisdictions?
questions.why_it_blocks: A rewards programme with real money raises contest, tax and licensing questions that cannot be assumed.
questions.known_information: The owner asked for rewards for top-performing strategies. No jurisdiction, entity, funding source or terms were supplied.
questions.what_would_answer_it: A written contest structure plus jurisdiction-specific legal review.
questions.source_note: The NFL Gambling Policy caps permissible prizes at $250 in related contests for NFL Personnel and prohibits personnel from sports-betting operations — a constraint on who can enter and how rewards may be framed.

questions.question: Will any NFL personnel (player, coach, staff) be permitted to enter strategies?
questions.why_it_blocks: League policy bars personnel from betting on NFL games and from sports-betting operations. If entrants could be personnel, the whole competition's compliance posture changes.
questions.known_information: The NFL Gambling Policy prohibits NFL Personnel from placing, soliciting or facilitating any bet on any NFL game, and prohibits using inside information.
questions.what_would_answer_it: An eligibility rule that explicitly excludes NFL Personnel, or a legal opinion that the structure is compliant.
questions.source_note: Section 2, 'Betting on Football' and 'Inside Information and Tipping'.

questions.question: Which markets are in scope for originating lines — spread, total, moneyline, team total, player props, alternates?
questions.why_it_blocks: Each market needs a different distribution model. Committing to props before having a distribution model produces fabricated numbers.
questions.known_information: The requirement names single bets, parlays and player-prop combinations.
questions.what_would_answer_it: A declared Season 0 market list.
questions.source_note: Rulebook defines the game statistics that props settle on; it does not define the market list.

questions.question: Do we have enough joint historical outcomes to publish a correlation value?
questions.why_it_blocks: Correlation values are required for prop-combo pricing. Inventing them would be the single worst failure in this project.
questions.known_information: Detecting rho = 0.10 at 80% power needs roughly 780+ paired observations before conditioning; a season is 272 games.
questions.what_would_answer_it: Multiple seasons of joint player-market outcomes under license.
questions.source_note: No joint-outcome dataset exists in the repo; the only verified data is the current-week snapshot.

questions.question: What is the bankroll, the staking rule, and the maximum acceptable drawdown?
questions.why_it_blocks: Gate 5 (risk of ruin) cannot be evaluated without a staking rule, so no strategy can be ranked on risk.
questions.known_information: No bankroll or staking rule has been supplied.
questions.what_would_answer_it: A stated bankroll and a pre-registered staking rule.
questions.source_note: Internal decision; no external source can supply it.

questions.question: What is the first scored window, and when does it open and close?
questions.why_it_blocks: Gates must be registered before the window opens. Without dates, nothing can be scored honestly.
questions.known_information: The 2026 season is in Week 10; Weeks 11-18 remain in the regular season.
questions.what_would_answer_it: A calendar decision recorded with a timestamp.
questions.source_note: Official schedule confirms current week and remaining regular-season structure.

questions.question: Which official source grades a settled bet, and how are stat corrections handled?
questions.why_it_blocks: If the grader and the settlement rule disagree, results become contestable and the leaderboard loses authority.
questions.known_information: Official box scores are the primary record of on-field results.
questions.what_would_answer_it: A named grading source plus a stat-correction policy with a revision window.
questions.source_note: Official game page carries the final box score used for grading.

questions.question: Do we collect depth charts for all 32 clubs, and at what cost in effort?
questions.why_it_blocks: The availability model is only comparable across teams if every club is covered. A 5-club pilot cannot support cross-team features.
questions.known_information: This release covers 5 clubs (BUF, SEA, DET, GB, BAL). 27 remain.
questions.what_would_answer_it: A capture schedule per club plus a storage format decision.
questions.source_note: One of the five club charts captured; the pattern is repeatable per club.

questions.question: May we publish originated lines publicly, and with what disclaimer?
questions.why_it_blocks: Publishing prices invites reliance. The wording of the disclaimer and any jurisdiction gating is a legal question.
questions.known_information: No publishing policy has been set. The dashboard publishes no prices; the research lab prices strategies against a named third-party closing line and says so on every row.
questions.what_would_answer_it: A written publishing policy, reviewed for the jurisdictions served.
questions.source_note: Internal decision; no external source can supply it.

questions.question: What does success look like numerically in Season 0, and who decides a strategy is promoted?
questions.why_it_blocks: Without a target, the board cannot say whether the project worked; and promotion authority must rest with someone accountable.
questions.known_information: Gates define per-strategy thresholds; no portfolio-level target exists.
questions.what_would_answer_it: A target (e.g. number of strategies clearing Gate 2 with n_eff >= 400) and a named arbiter.
questions.source_note: Internal decision; no external source can supply it.

questions.question: How often may the published tables be refreshed, and how is staleness displayed?
questions.why_it_blocks: Injury and schedule data decay within days. A table with no visible timestamp is misleading even when every value was once correct.
questions.known_information: Every table in this release carries the 2026-11-14 retrieval date.
questions.what_would_answer_it: A refresh schedule and a staleness banner rule.
questions.source_note: The official report is week-specific and changes daily; staleness is therefore guaranteed without a cadence.

questions.question: Is the official Week 10 injury report complete for all 14 games?
questions.why_it_blocks: A partially captured report would bias any availability feature toward the games that were captured.
questions.known_information: All 14 Week 10 games and all 28 participating clubs are present in the captured report; 345 player rows were transcribed.
questions.answer: Yes for the captured snapshot: every week-10 game and every participating club has rows, verified mechanically by tools/verify_data.py (2,944 checks).
questions.what_would_answer_it: A second independent capture compared row-for-row to confirm nothing was missed in transcription.
questions.source_note: Coverage check is internal consistency, not a second independent transcription — hence 'partially'.

questions.question: Which source will be accepted as the official price feed for the market open/close columns of the snapshot store?
questions.why_it_blocks: The store now records our own line for every originated market, but market_line and difference stay blank until a source is named. No CLV, no ROI, no fair-vs-market column can fill without it.
questions.known_information: No league or club source publishes betting prices (flag F-06). The repository carries a fingerprinted third-party mirror whose line provenance is undocumented (flag I-10). The store itself is built and published: 84 records, open/close stages, blank-and-flag behaviour enforced by tools/build_snapshots.py.
questions.answer: Partial. The schema, stages and capture rules are decided; the feed itself is not. The realistic options are (a) one named book, (b) a consensus service, (c) the owner's own account statements — official for the owner's P&L but not a market number.
questions.what_would_answer_it: Owner picks a tier and supplies access; market_line and difference then fill from recorded captures only, never from memory.
questions.source_note: Snapshot store as published this round

questions.question: What unattended job captures the close snapshot at kickoff for every originated market?
questions.why_it_blocks: Without it the close half of the store never fills: this round recorded 39 open captures and 39 close captures marked pending_kickoff, and the one already-played game is flagged not_captured_before_kickoff.
questions.known_information: The snapshot clock is 2026-11-14, after the Week 10 Thursday kickoff (2026-11-12), so that game's captures are post-hoc and are flagged rather than back-dated (flag F-14). The repo already runs data-refresh.yml every 6 hours.
questions.answer: Partial. The capture mechanics and the status vocabulary (recorded / pending_kickoff / not_captured_before_kickoff) are defined; no job yet runs them at kickoff.
questions.what_would_answer_it: A kickoff-timestamped step in the scheduled workflow that re-runs tools/build_snapshots.py with a capture flag and commits the result.
questions.source_note: Store contract and capture rules

questions.question: What exact measured decay sends a live strategy back to paper under gate G8?
questions.why_it_blocks: A demotion gate with no ratified numbers is a description, not a control. Nothing may leave paper until the thresholds are fixed in advance.
questions.known_information: G8 was added to data/gates.json this round with four proposed triggers: rolling z < 1.0 over 100 graded bets; two consecutive gate re-run failures; median max drawdown > 25% of bankroll; mean CLV <= 0 over 50 bets. No strategy is live, so the gate is defined but not active.
questions.answer: Partial. The trigger families are chosen; the numbers are proposals. They must be ratified before promotion, never after — changing a gate after results exist is itself a gate violation.
questions.what_would_answer_it: Owner accepts or edits the four thresholds in data/gates.json G8 and stamps the ratification date.
questions.source_note: Root gate register including the new G8

questions.question: Should the signal group be graded against a 50% baseline or against the break-even implied by the price?
questions.why_it_blocks: A hit rate above 50% is not an edge if the price demands 52.4%. The leaderboard split needs one rule before strategies are compared to each other.
questions.known_information: With no official price there is no break-even to measure against (Q-19). ST-11 is therefore graded against 0.50 and every row says so: 84-49 on 133 decided games, z=3.04, p=0.0024, computed from official results only.
questions.answer: Partial. 50% is the only defensible baseline while prices are blocked; the rule must switch to price break-even — publishing both columns — as soon as Q-19 resolves.
questions.what_would_answer_it: Q-19 resolution, then recompute signal_z against break-even and keep the 50% figure as a secondary column.
questions.source_note: Signal grade and its stated baseline

questions.question: Which model is the origination of record when the two in-repo models disagree?
questions.why_it_blocks: Two models publish lines for the same games. The snapshot store and the origination-order table cite one of them; a fair/market/difference column is meaningless if 'fair' can mean two different numbers.
questions.known_information: Model A (code/build_lines.py ratings) posts WAS -0.5 for the Week 10 Thursday game; model B (research-lab walk-forward Poisson) posts home margin +3.09, i.e. WAS -3.09. Both files are in the repository with their own diagnostics; neither has been designated the origin of record.
questions.answer: Open. This round's snapshot store uses model A because it is the file that originates side, total and moneyline together; model B is used for the ST-11 signal grade. The split is documented, not decided.
questions.what_would_answer_it: Owner designates one model of record for origination; the other becomes a published cross-check with its own column.
questions.source_note: Week 10 origination file (model A)

questions.question: How does the results feed stay current without a person re-reading the schedule pages?
questions.why_it_blocks: The feed is the foundation of every backtest. If it silently goes stale, ROI computed on it is wrong without anyone noticing.
questions.known_information: This round's 137 rows were produced by line-by-line reads of official by-week pages and verified three ways (row diff vs mirror, standings arithmetic, source-URL audit). The scheduled data-refresh workflow re-pulls standings, injuries and team stats every 6 hours but does not yet re-read results.
questions.answer: Partial. The verification path is proven and repeatable; the scheduled refresh does not yet include it.
questions.what_would_answer_it: Add a by-week results step to data-refresh.yml (GitHub Actions can reach nfl.com) that re-reads completed weeks and re-runs tools/build_results.py checks, failing loudly on any mismatch.
questions.source_note: Results feed builder and its three checks
